exposure: type of lower uterine Caesarean section (elective or emergency)
outcome: surgical site infections (SSIs) after lower uterine Caesarean section
cohort: The study included 687 patients who developed surgical site infections after lower uterine caesarean sections in Western Australian public hospitals from 2001 to 2021.
finding: The most common organisms causing surgical site infections after lower uterine caesarean sections were MSSA, MRSA, Enterobacterales, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Staphylococcus lugdunensis, with SSIs being significantly more common after emergency LUCS.
mod_finding: Surgical site infections were significantly more common after emergency lower uterine caesarean sections compared to elective ones.
